content:
elena: Quick update — we're launching a small set of Hosted API changes tonight that touch streaming, tool-calling policies, and fallback behavior. TL;DR: new 'fast-lane' streaming endpoint for low-latency apps, an adaptive fallback playbook for capacity/backoff, and tightened per-tool call rate limits. Rolling canary starts 18:00 PT, broader rollout next Tue. :rocket:

matt: Nice. Can you add the canary targets? I'll wire alerts and cursors into the dashboard.

elena: Canary targets: 5% traffic in us-west-2 -> 18:00 PT, 20% in US regions 2h after if healthy. If canary latency P95 > 120ms or error rate > 0.8% we pause and auto-roll back.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for channel: hosted-fast-lane-canary at 1900501800. Jobs: canary-deploy-1872, health-check-1872.

kevin: Which metrics should oncall watch besides P95 and error? CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, and KV cache hit rate?

elena: Exactly. Watch list: P50/P95 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, GPU util, host queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, token throughput per-second. Also watch 'fallbacks.invoked' metric (we added this).

julia: Anything to note re: data plane or KMS? Customers on Private/Dedicated unaffected, right?

elena: Private/Dedicated unaffected by the default policy changes. For Hosted: tool-calling rate limits tightened to 15 calls/min per-tool per-key (from 30) to avoid thundering; customers on Dedicated can opt into the new policy or keep existing limits via support ticket. KMS unchanged.

nora: Docs PR opened -> https://git.internal/docs/hosted/fast-lane-playbook (will link changelog & migration notes). I'll push a short user-facing note for the dashboard feed.

matt: On the alert side I'll add an alert that triggers when fallback rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m and a runbook pointer. Runbook snippet:
```
When 'fallbacks.invoked' > 0.5% for 5m:
  1) Check canary-deploy health.
  2) Verify model pool capacity in us-west-2.
  3) If KV cache hit ratio < 40% consider cache warmup.
  4) If GPU util > 85% consider temporary scaling or rollback.
```

samir: How will the 'fast-lane' endpoint look in the API? Example request?

elena: Exposed as an opt-in endpoint: `POST /v2/fast-lane/stream` with same auth but needs header `X-Redwood-Low-Latency: 1`. It enforces shorter batching windows and prioritizes preemptive KV warm-up. Example: 
```http
POST /v2/fast-lane/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <key>
X-Redwood-Low-Latency: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{ "model": "mosaicx-fast-1", "input": "Summarize...", "max_tokens": 256 }
```

elena: Note: fast-lane pricing is the same as standard for now; it's a quality-of-service opt-in. We may introduce a premium tier later but will announce separately.

kevin: Any client-side guidance? Timeouts, retries?

elena: Yes — client tips: use shorter timeouts (1.5x expected latency), implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429/503, and respect the new per-tool rate headers we return: `X-Tool-Rate-Limit` and `X-Tool-Rate-Remaining`. We'll add code samples in the docs.

nora: I'll coordinate the user note and changelog: short banner + expanded doc. ETA: PR merged by EOD.

matt: I'll monitor dashboards during canary window and tag this thread if anything abnormal.

elena: Thanks everyone. If any product manager or legal folks want a quick sync, ping me. Expect final GA announcement early next week with a longer playbook and customer comms. :thumbsup:
